Outlet: CNBC (Reuters copy), published Fri Nov 6 2026 12:03 AM EST, updated Fri Nov 6 2026 1:06 PM EST
Gold drops 1% as strong U.S payrolls boost dollar, yields

Gold prices declined following robust U.S. employment data. Spot gold fell 0.7% to $4,059.90 an ounce, reaching a session low of $4,033.29. December gold futures dropped 1% to $4,071.80. Weekly gains stood at 4.8%.

The U.S. dollar strengthened 0.7% to its highest level since October 29, making gold costlier for foreign currency holders. Benchmark 10-year Treasury yields also increased.

Stronger-than-expected payrolls reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve could maintain elevated interest rates longer. U.S. nonfarm payrolls increased more than anticipated in October while the unemployment rate fell to 4.1%.

Traders now see a 74.8% probability of a Fed rate increase in December, compared to 72.8% prior to the employment report, per CME's FedWatch tool.

Tai Wong, independent metals trader: "Gold gapped lower on a stellar employment report (that was) strong across the board, but is trying to claw back higher."

Spot silver rose 0.2% to $51.88, platinum gained 1.2% to $1,534.59, and palladium fell 0.9% to $1,021.50. All three showed weekly gains.

Lower gold prices spurred Indian retail purchasing ahead of the Diwali festival. Gold had reached a one-year low of $3,869.85 per ounce on October 30.
